rv.q: It’s dangerous, surprising, and wildly entertaining.
Even when Barnes overstates his case, as he does by having Jack assume the role of a serial killer, the play is held together by McAvoy's mesmerising performance.
McAvoy's journey through the play's different moods is a tour de force.
Barnes’s play needs him. It clobbers its jokes to death.

cn.t: McAvoy's magnetic performance is the undisputed highlight of this uneven but bold revival. Barnes's blunt 1968 class satire feels occasionally overblown, yet its dark comedy lands with chilling relevance.
